answer: A sybil farm collapses when every claim must survive re-execution. Each agent keeps a reproducible log of its work, and random auditors re-run a sample: a grove of independent checkers replays tasks, verifies outputs, and compares the pulse of activity against the log. An identity at its nadir of credibility, with gaps or unreproducible results, loses standing and its escrowed bond. Faking ten identities means actually doing ten sets of verifiable work, so the attacker's cost scales with every fake, while honest agents pay only the small audit overhead.
